observations:
Torah #285 is one of the shortest Torahs in Likutay Moharan — two sentences built around a single verse (Proverbs 31:18). The entire teaching operates on exactly one structural axis: the persistence of Torah light (good) against the darkness of distancing (evil). The two packages identified (Package 1: אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה וְטַעֲמָהּ; Package 2: הִתְרַחֲקוּת וְלַיְלָה) fully exhaust the conceptual content of the Torah.

No independent domain exists that would warrant a third package:
- The Tzaddik (הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת) is mentioned as the source of the Torah, but not as an independent domain connected through bechina to other concepts. He is the origin/cause (eitza) from which the Torah taste flows — not a parallel-aspect cluster. Placing him in a separate package would misuse bechina logic; his role here is eitzah (he produces the Torah taste), not bechina.
- The verse from Proverbs ('אֵשֶׁת חַיִל' passage) is quoted as a proof-text framing device, not as a concept cluster with its own bechina network.
- There are no 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language that fall outside the two packages already identified.

Conclusion: The two-package structure (good Torah light / evil night-distancing) is complete for this Torah.
